Meltdown: Every Intel CPU since the original Pentium (I) CPU. 10 years or more of this "design flaw". This Intel flaw cannot be "fixed" without a performance penalty. How much of a performance penalty is dependent on how often your CPU is making syscalls which are calls to the Operating System for something outside of the program's control. Spectre: Two types of attacks. Most CPUs with branch prediction have possibility of being affected.

Spectre can affect Intel in more than one way and this patch will likely be at the BIOS level, maybe in conjunction with an Operating System patch. Nothing released yet. Unknown if one of the variants can be patched on Intel.

Spectre is low likelihood of affecting AMD (of the two variants, only 1 method, on only 2 types of CPUs with non-default Linux configurations has been shown). BIOS patch in the works. According to AMD the patch will have no impact on performance.

If you run Linux on AMD, you will not be slowed down by the Intel Meltdown patch
